prompt: Let $T=8$. $a:b=1:2$, $b:c=3:4$, $c:d=5:6$ and $d:a=x:(T+12)$. Find the value of $x$.

solutions.title: Chain the ratios
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from A1; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) Multiplying the ratios, $\frac ad=\frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56=\frac5{16}$, so $\frac da=\frac{16}5$. Then $\frac x{20}=\frac{16}5$ and $x=64$.

**Answer: $64$**

prompt: Let $T=105$. The sequence $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ is defined by $a_1=1$, $a_2=T$ and, for $n>1$, $a_{n+1}=\dfrac{a_n}{a_{n-1}}$. Find the value of $a_{2021}$.

solutions.title: Find the period
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from A3; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) The terms are $a_1=1$, $a_2=T$, $a_3=T$, $a_4=1$, $a_5=\frac1T$, $a_6=\frac1T$, $a_7=1$, $a_8=T$. Since $a_7=a_1$ and $a_8=a_2$, the sequence repeats with period $6$. $2021=6\cdot336+5$, so $a_{2021}=a_5=\frac1T=\frac1{105}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{105}$**

prompt: Let $T=25$. A cylinder has volume $240\ \text{cm}^3$ and surface area $120\ \text{cm}^2$. A similar cylinder has volume $1200T\ \text{cm}^3$ and surface area $24k^3\ \text{cm}^2$. Find the value of $k$.

solutions.title: Scale factors
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from B1; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) The second cylinder has volume $30000$, which is $125$ times $240$, so the linear scale factor is $5$ and the surface area is $25\cdot120=3000$. Then $24k^3=3000$, $k^3=125$ and $k=5$.

**Answer: $5$**

prompt: Let $T=5$. $A=\left(\dfrac14\right)^{\frac T2}\times\left(\dfrac18\right)^{\frac23}\times\left(\dfrac1{16}\right)^{-\frac34}\times\left(\dfrac1{64}\right)^{-\frac56}$ and $B=27^{-\frac23}\times9^{\frac T2}\times81^{-\frac34}$. Find the value of $A+B$.

solutions.title: Write everything in powers of 2 and 3
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from B2; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) $A=2^{-2\cdot\frac52}\cdot2^{-3\cdot\frac23}\cdot2^{4\cdot\frac34}\cdot2^{6\cdot\frac56}=2^{-5-2+3+5}=2^1=2$. $B=3^{3\cdot(-\frac23)}\cdot3^{2\cdot\frac52}\cdot3^{4\cdot(-\frac34)}=3^{-2+5-3}=3^0=1$. So $A+B=3$.

**Answer: $3$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (National Final)
source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question C1

prompt: $m$, $m+2$, $m+6$ and $m+8$ are all prime numbers, with $m>11$. Find the least possible value of $m$.

solutions.title: Use remainders mod 5
solutions.body:
Look at the numbers modulo $5$. If $m\equiv0,2,3,4\pmod5$, then one of $m$, $m+2$, $m+6$, $m+8$ is a multiple of $5$ (for $m\equiv2$: $m+8$; $m\equiv3$: $m+2$; $m\equiv4$: $m+6$; $m\equiv0$: $m$) and larger than $5$, so not prime. Hence $m\equiv1\pmod5$, and $m$ is odd, so $m\equiv1\pmod{10}$. Checking $m=21,31,41,\dots$ ($m>11$): $31$ ($31,33$ no), $41$ ($49$ no), $61$ ($63$ no), $71$ ($77$ no), $81$ not prime, $91$ not prime, and $101,103,107,109$ are all prime.

**Answer: $101$**

source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question C2

prompt: Let $T=101$. Five integers are such that the range is $T-1$ more than the mean, the mean is $T-1$ more than the median, and the median is $T-1$ more than the mode. $9(T-1)$ is the largest of the five integers. Find the mean of the other four integers.

solutions.title: Set up with the mode
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C1; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) Here $T-1=100$ and the largest integer is $900$. Let the mode be $m$; then the median is $m+100$, the mean is $m+200$ and the range is $m+300$, so the smallest integer is $900-(m+300)=600-m$. Order the integers $x_1\le x_2\le x_3\le x_4\le x_5=900$ with $x_1=600-m$ and $x_3=m+100$. The mode $m$ occurs at least twice and is less than the median, so $m=x_1=x_2$, giving $600-m=m$, $m=300$. Then $x_1=x_2=300$, $x_3=400$, and the sum is $5\cdot500=2500$, so $x_4=2500-300-300-400-900=600$. The mean of the other four integers is $\frac{300+300+400+600}4=400$.

**Answer: $400$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (National Final)
source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question C3

prompt: Let $T=400$. Four vertices of a regular octagon are joined to form a square. The length of each side of the octagon is $\sqrt T$. Find the area of the square in the form $a+\sqrt b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Find the value of $a+b$.

solutions.title: Area of the inscribed square
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C2; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) The octagon has side $s=\sqrt{400}=20$. The square joins alternate vertices. If the octagon has circumradius $R$, then $s=2R\sin22.5^\circ$ and the square has side $R\sqrt2$, so its area is $2R^2=\frac{s^2}{2\sin^222.5^\circ}$. Since $\sin^222.5^\circ=\frac{1-\cos45^\circ}2=\frac{2-\sqrt2}4$, the area is $\frac{2s^2}{2-\sqrt2}=s^2(2+\sqrt2)=400(2+\sqrt2)=800+400\sqrt2=800+\sqrt{320000}$.

So $a=800$, $b=320000$ and $a+b=320800$.

**Answer: $320800$**

solutions.title: Law of cosines
solutions.body:
Two adjacent sides of the octagon, each of length $s=20$, meet at an interior angle of $135^\circ$. The side of the square joins the two outer ends of these sides, so its length $\ell$ satisfies $\ell^2=s^2+s^2-2s^2\cos135^\circ=s^2(2+\sqrt2)$. The area of the square is $\ell^2=400(2+\sqrt2)=800+\sqrt{320000}$, so $a+b=320800$.

**Answer: $320800$**

prompt: Let $T=320800$. Let $x\diamond y=\sqrt{x^2+4y^2-4xy}$. Find the value of $(T\diamond3)\diamond5$.

solutions.title: Simplify the operation
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C3; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) $x^2+4y^2-4xy=(x-2y)^2$, so $x\diamond y=|x-2y|$. Then $T\diamond3=|320800-6|=320794$ and $320794\diamond5=|320794-10|=320784$.

**Answer: $320784$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (National Final)
source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question D1

prompt: $x$, $y$ and $z$ are positive integers with $x<y<z$, and $x+2xy+3xyz=71$. Find the value of $z$.

solutions.title: Factor
solutions.body:
$x(1+2y+3yz)=71$, and $71$ is prime, so $x=1$ ($x=71$ is impossible since $1+2y+3yz>1$). Then $2y+3yz=70$, i.e. $y(2+3z)=70$ with $1<y<z$. The divisors of $70$ with $y\ge2$: $y=2$ gives $2+3z=35$, $z=11$ ✓ ($y<z$). $y=5$ gives $2+3z=14$, $z=4<y$ ✗; $y=7$ gives $3z=8$ ✗; $y=10,14,\dots$ give $2+3z\le7$, so $z\le1$ ✗.

**Answer: $11$**

prompt: Let $T=11$. $x+\dfrac1x=T$. $x^3+\dfrac1{x^3}$ is the four-digit integer '$abcd$'. Find the value of $(a+c)-(b+d)$. (Hint: $(p+q)^3=p^3+3p^2q+3pq^2+q^3$.)

solutions.title: Cube the relation
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D1; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) $\left(x+\frac1x\right)^3=x^3+\frac1{x^3}+3\left(x+\frac1x\right)$, so $x^3+\frac1{x^3}=T^3-3T=1331-33=1298$. Then $(a+c)-(b+d)=(1+9)-(2+8)=0$.

**Answer: $0$**

source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question D3

prompt: Let $T=0$. $BFDC$ is a rectangle and $AFE$ is a straight line. Also $AF=AB=(3+T)$ cm, $\angle BAF=\angle DEF=90^\circ$ and $\angle BFC=60^\circ$. The length of $DE$ is $\sqrt k$ cm. Find the value of $k+T$.

solutions.title: Angle chase
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D2; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) Here $AF=AB=3$. Triangle $ABF$ is a right isosceles triangle, so $BF=3\sqrt2$ and $\angle AFB=45^\circ$. In the rectangle, $\angle BFC=60^\circ$ and $\angle CBF=90^\circ$, so $BC=BF\tan60^\circ=3\sqrt6$, and $FD=BC=3\sqrt6$. On the line $AFE$: $\angle AFB+\angle BFD+\angle DFE=180^\circ$, so $\angle DFE=180-45-90=45^\circ$. Triangle $DEF$ has a right angle at $E$ and a $45^\circ$ angle, so $DE=\frac{FD}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt3$ and $DE^2=27$, $k=27$. Then $k+T=27$.

**Answer: $27$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (National Final)
source.paper: 2019-20 National Final, Shuttle Round, question D4

prompt: Let $T=27$. The simultaneous equations $x^2+Txy+\dfrac{T^2}4y^2=729$ and $x^2+\dfrac T2xy+\dfrac{T^2}{16}y^2=225$ have four solution pairs $(x,y)$. Find the sum of the two positive values of $y$.

solutions.title: Perfect squares
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D3; no official answers were published for this round, so the chain is worked out here.) The left sides are $\left(x+\frac T2y\right)^2=729$ and $\left(x+\frac T4y\right)^2=225$. So $x+\frac{27}2y=\pm27$ and $x+\frac{27}4y=\pm15$. Subtracting the second from the first: $\frac{27}4y=(\pm27)-(\pm15)$, so $y=\frac4{27}\cdot\{12,42,-42,-12\}=\frac{16}9,\frac{56}9,-\frac{56}9,-\frac{16}9$. The positive values are $\frac{16}9$ and $\frac{56}9$, with sum $\frac{72}9=8$.

**Answer: $8$**
